subject: Running INLA remotely - problem with inlarc file?

messages.author: a3528cfc1d2614c7
messages.subject: Running INLA remotely - problem with inlarc file?
parts:
Hi,

I am trying to run INLA remotely from my Linux laptop (running R in RStudio, not sure if that matters). I have generated and edited ~/.inlarc to the specifications for the server I am trying to access, but when I run with the remote call, somehow I get...

Run /usr/local/bin/inla at go...@inla.math.ntnu.no

My username has somehow transferred...but the server hasn't changed?? Also, the path to the file is not the one in .inlarc - I double-checked that it was the right file path, etc. Do I also have to change the .inlarc file on the remote host?

Any ideas?
--Jess

### The name of the remote host.
#RemoteHost="server.dept.campus.edu" #of course I put in a fake name

### The username on the remote host
#RemoteUser="gorzo"

### Full path to the inla-program on the remote host
#RemoteINLA="/usr/local/bin/R/x86-64/inla64"

### Arguments to ssh. Usually no need to change this
#sshArguments="-x -o BatchMode=yes -o TCPKeepAlive=yes -e none"

### Port number
#Port=22


Yet, for some reason, it still pulls the details I posted originally, namely, the original settings. (Oddly, it saves my user name.)

comment like. then the variable RemoteHost will be set. this is also
the case for the other variables.

messages.author: b453c29749de564d
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Running INLA remotely - problem with inlarc file?
parts:
On Tue, 2015-10-06 at 08:01 -0700, Jessica Gorzo wrote:
> Ah, really sorry for my sloppy post. I copied this template from
> online to show the example, but I'm pretty sure I un-commentend them
> in my file at home. I will double-check when I get back though; it
> was a late night of R after all ;)

if so, then you'll need help of some local linux-person, as this is
just a matter of setting up the ssh-connection password free. also you
need to provide the correct path to the inla-binary program, like if
you're using the one in the R-INLA package, then do

> INLA:::inla.call.builtin()
[1] "/home/hrue/R/x86_64-redhat-linux-gnu-library/3.2/INLA/bin/linux/in
la64"

and use that as the value for 'RemoteINLA'
